video_title: We Have A Game 7! Wemby vs SGA For A Trip To The Finals! Road Trippin' In The Morning

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins defends Shai Gilgeous-Alexander against recent criticism
quotes.excerpt: People are actually playing and fucking with this man's name and his legacy at this moment.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: People are like, oh, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, he's soft as shit. I'm like, no, people are actually playing and fucking with this man's name and his legacy at this moment. The criticism that he's getting is not warranted. Everyone, let's make it clear, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander sells calls like everybody else does in the league at times. But this guy has been averaging 30 for the last four years and we talked about this time and time again, shooting 50% from the field. He led the league in tough contested made two-point shots outside the paint.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: Well, I'm not going to sit here and talk about, oh, they were too aggressive on Wembanyama. Oh, did we -- we're going to talk about those hits on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander? Or did you see -- yes, welcome, welcome. If you know the history of basketball, this is consistent.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the difference between regular season and playoff officiating
quotes.excerpt: Just because we all watch it one way during the regular season, the playoffs, this shit is different.
quotes.quote: Just because we all watch it one way during the regular season, the playoffs, this shit is different. And it's like, just because we all watch it one way during the regular season, and there's fans or analysts that want to like, oh, Victor Wembanyama threw an elbow. Oh my god, eight days of coverage and Victor Wembanyama threw an elbow. And everybody that's been in those games is like, bow down time, motherfucker threw an elbow, because they were going to keep doing it until he did it. I'd have thrown an elbow sooner, just to send a message.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins predicts Oklahoma City Thunder role players will respond at home
quotes.excerpt: Role players play better at home. We keep saying that, but it's been a real thing.
quotes.quote: I'm leaning more towards Oklahoma City Thunder, and the reason being is because what we've witnessed in Game 4, Game 5, Game 6 is role players play better at home. We keep saying that, but it's been a real thing in this series. The role players stepped up at the crib. Dylan Harper had a bad -- by the way, shout out to Dylan Harper, because I picked you on our group thing, baby. Fanatics Sportsbook, eight and a half points, you had that shit in the first half, I believe. But look, they play better at home. I believe Oklahoma City Thunder role players are going to respond at home. They have no choice.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Victor Wembanyama's unique ability to take over games
quotes.excerpt: Victor Wembanyama is currently the one human being on the planet that when he is at his peak.
quotes.quote: Victor Wembanyama is currently the one human being on the planet that when he is at his peak, there's no human that can do anything about it. There's no human. He's a Shaquille O'Neal, he's a LeBron James, he's a Stephen Curry from three. When he gets going, we're all, we're all watching. I'm, I'm as helpless sitting on my couch as the defenders on the court.

quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.summary_phrase: Allie Clifton on the importance of response games in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: One of my favorite things in watching a competitor is their response game.
quotes.quote: One of my favorite things in watching a competitor is their response game. And it's different than in the regular season when you're coming off of a loss. It's different when you're in the postseason and you're doing it as each round gets tougher and tougher. And you can say what you want about overseas and that play, but also you're going against the defending champs, you're going against one of the deepest teams, one of the most successful squads that we're talking are on the verge of this dynasty. And so I still think that there was a thought process there of how he would respond in a situation like that.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on the historical significance of the Spurs-Thunder series
quotes.excerpt: It is a legacy moment this Game 7 for both Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Victor Wembanyama.
quotes.quote: It is a legacy moment this Game 7 for both Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Victor Wembanyama. For Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, you got to defend your home court. You've been struggling, they've been having you on lock, you've been shooting your worst that you ever did in any series percentage-wise. For Victor Wembanyama, hey big fellow, you got a chance, you've been doing a lot of barking and some biting, but you've been doing a lot of barking. The world know you hate these people. You said in regular season you dominated them, now you're going into the chips, a hostile environment, you can't wet the bed.

quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.summary_phrase: Allie Clifton on the rarity of winning MVP and a championship in back-to-back seasons
quotes.excerpt: Only three players in NBA history have achieved this rare feat of winning both the regular season MVP.
quotes.quote: Only three players in NBA history have achieved this rare feat of winning both the regular season MVP and an NBA championship in back-to-back seasons. Who are they? You are correct with Bill Russell, Jordan. Is it Magic? No, it's after Jordan.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the criticism of James Harden's playoff success
quotes.excerpt: The whole criticism about James Harden is we don't have experience in watching him be successful.
quotes.quote: The whole criticism about James Harden is we don't have experience in watching him be successful in certain moments. So then that's where, where in the criticism lies. Donovan Mitchell, I don't have experience watching him go to the conference finals, so it's hard for me after this time to pick him to go to the conference finals because he's never done it.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the 'don't count out the champ' rule
quotes.excerpt: You don't count out the champ until they've been beaten. Why? Because they are a champion.
quotes.quote: You don't count out the champ until they've been beaten. Why? Because they are a champion and their experience has proven I will never count out a champion. They have given me an experience to watch them be in that space, so I'm not going to question them until they're beaten. They are the defending champs and I will give them that respect.

quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.summary_phrase: Allie Clifton reports on Mitchell Robinson's finger surgery
quotes.excerpt: New York Knicks center Mitchell Robinson underwent surgery on his right pinky finger he broke earlier this week.
quotes.quote: New York Knicks center Mitchell Robinson underwent surgery on his right pinky finger he broke earlier this week. The team is hopeful he can return for Game 1 of the NBA Finals, which starts on Wednesday.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the NBA's plan to use AI for officiating
quotes.excerpt: NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said the league will use AI to automate a category of calls.
quotes.quote: NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said the league will use AI to automate a category of calls such as out-of-bounds decisions to speed up games and reduce disputes over possession. Silver compared the system to the Hawk-Eye technology used in tennis where electronic line calling quickly determines whether a ball has landed in or out. Silver said, we're going to move to a system like that where that whole category of calls will be automatic. It will take all those so-called objective calls out of the hands of the referees. You won't have to deal with challenges on those calls.
